t: This is 10 Trinity Square, a Grade II* listed building at Tower Hill, in the southeastern corner of the City of London, overlooking the River Thames. It's built in the Beaux Arts style, and it's best known as the former headquarters of the Port of London Authority, so you'll sometimes hear it called the Port of London Authority Building. The architect was Sir Edwin Cooper, whose work has been described as essentially Classical, and sometimes powerfully Baroque. Today the building is a hotel.
